reason: XnView MP already opens every RAW and file type I throw at it, so NuViewer's extra formats don't fix anything for me. I'd install the portable zip to see if it really is faster on a 500-shot card, but nothing here tells me it helps with culling.
why_switch_or_not: I switch the moment an app opens something my current one fails on, and NuViewer's 26 of 32 formats doesn't show me a file XnView chokes on in my work (RAW, PSD, TIFF, the odd AVIF). The listed features mention no ratings, flags, colour labels or reject-and-delete workflow for culling, and I'd have to rebuild my shortcuts and file associations by hand for a 0.4.1 from one person. Speed is the only real pull, and the numbers are for JPG/PNG on his PC, not 45 MP RAW files off my card.
current_app_pros: XnView MP is a browser, batch converter and metadata tool in one. It opens nearly everything, handles RAW+JPG folders and IPTC/EXIF/XMP, and I already have my rating and labelling shortcuts and my batch convert presets set up.
current_app_pains: It's sluggish when I flick through big RAW files, and the thumbnail cache gets slow on a fresh 500-file card. The interface is cluttered too. None of it is bad enough to make me leave.
objection: I'd have to relearn shortcuts and reset file associations for a one-man 0.4.1, and I can't see anything for rating or rejecting shots, which is what I do all day. RAW and JPG always showing separately is fine for viewing but doesn't tell me how pair culling works.
would_change_my_mind: Fast full-size RAW flipping that I can measure on my own 500-shot card, with star/colour ratings or a reject mark that writes XMP sidecars my other software reads, and a file type it opens that XnView fails on.
